I will keep my full 18 mu in the usual wheat-maize rotation, because that is the system I know best and it fits my land, labor, and well irrigation. I have farmed for 40 years, so I do not want to take unnecessary risks. For winter wheat, I will use improved seed, put in a moderate but solid fertilizer rate, irrigate several times with the well, and manage weeds and disease with a few pesticide sprays so I can protect yield. After wheat harvest, I will plant summer maize on the same 18 mu. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because I care most about stable production, and I will keep fertilizer and irrigation at a practical level that matches my labor and water access. Because my household is small and some labor is off-farm, I will choose straightforward field operations and rotary tillage rather than heavier, slower work. My goal is steady grain yield from both crops instead of chasing very high input production.
